SUHAKAM reports that stateless children face lack of identity documents, school-admission delays or denial, and high medical costs or denial of care. At least one Article 15A case documented by SUHAKAM ran 11 years before resolution.
Citizenship granted by undocumented substantive discretion is not citizenship. It is favour. The fix is publishing success criteria, not amending the article.

After the 2024 maternal-citizenship amendment, transparency on Article 15A discretion remains the next reform: published criteria, statutory deadlines, disaggregated outcomes.

entries.headline: SUHAKAM-Linked 2022 Estimates: 500,000 to 1 Million Stateless Children in Sabah

posts.text: SUHAKAM-linked 2022 reporting estimates 500,000 to 1 million stateless children in Sabah. There is no official figure.

Federal Constitution Article 14 grants citizenship by birth under specific conditions. Stateless children fall through gaps in jus soli and jus sanguinis. The conditions assume parental documentation many lack, perpetuating statelessness across generations.
Malaysia is not bound by the 1961 Statelessness Convention. It is a party to the CRC with reservations affecting Article 7 (right to acquire nationality).

The Bajau Laut are a frequently cited affected group, described by researchers as 'genuinely stateless' across Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines. Many Bajau Laut have lived along Sabah's coast for generations; no state recognises them as citizens.
UNICEF's Sabah study found 18,781 'invisible' children missing from official databases. SUHAKAM-linked reporting estimates the latent stateless population at 500K-1M.

Statelessness in Sabah is structural exclusion. It needs citizenship-pathway legislation and the will to count the affected population honestly.

entries.headline: Suaram: 6,892 SOSMA Arrests Since 2012; Reported 20–28% Released Without Charge

posts.text: Suaram: 6,892 SOSMA arrests since 2012; reported 20-28% released without any charge filed. Of arrests under the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012 since enactment, between a fifth and just over a quarter were reported to result in no charge.
SOSMA Section 4 allows 28 days of pre-charge police detention since 2012. The Act replaced the ISA but retains extended investigative-detention powers.
SUHAKAM announced a public inquiry in 2025 into alleged human rights violations linked to a 17 January 2025 Taiping Prison incident that led to a death in custody.
Suaram's annual reports are a regularly cited civil-society source on SOSMA usage. Disaggregated official reporting remains limited.
SOSMA is a routine pre-charge detention regime. Suaram's reported 20-28% release-without-charge rate is the live editorial fact, not a one-time anomaly.
Like a 28-day holding cell where one in four to five occupants is released with no charge, and there is no fully disaggregated public log of who entered or why.

Genuine SOSMA reform requires disaggregated public reporting on arrests, durations, charges and outcomes, not just renewal debates every five years.

entries.headline: Kampung Baru Master Redevelopment Remains Unrealised; PKB Has Delivered Smaller Projects

posts.text: Forty years of proposals, no master redevelopment delivered. PKB lists completed smaller projects; the comprehensive plan has not begun.
Kampung Baru sits beside the KLCC core. The land has Malay Agricultural Settlement status with Malay-only ownership restrictions.

PKB's 2010 census recorded 18,372 residents. Many trace household ties to the 1899 founding of the settlement. Heritage value is officially recognised. PKB plans envisage phased redevelopment with Malay ownership safeguards and heritage protections built into design.
PKB (Perbadanan Pembangunan Kampong Bharu), set up in 2012, has delivered specific projects but not the comprehensive master redevelopment.
Kampung Baru is not a real estate problem. It is the unresolved question of whether Malay heritage and KLCC-grade land economics can coexist on the same blocks.
Like a historic neighbourhood where the heirs and the city disagree on renovation: four decades of blueprints, only patchwork delivery.

The path forward is not a bigger plan. It is structured smaller-block consolidation with heritage and Malay-ownership protections built into each phase.

entries.headline: Malaysia's 2024 Deficit 4.1%, 2025 Came In at 3.7%; PFFRA Targets Frame the Glide Path
entries.radarSignal: pac urges stricter procurement safeguards at mahb in early review of privatisation.

posts.text: Malaysia narrowed its deficit to 4.1% in 2024 and 3.7% in 2025, beating the 3.8% projection. The PFFRA medium-term target is 3% of GDP.

Every 1 percentage point of deficit adds tens of billions to annual borrowing. Long-term sustainability requires revenue mobilisation (broader SST, CGT) or sustained spending discipline. Both involve political trade-offs.
Credit rating outlooks track consistent target performance. Downgrades are associated with higher yields and risk premia across the sovereign curve.

The Public Finance and Fiscal Responsibility Act 2023 (Act 850) provides statutory fiscal objectives and a 3-to-5-year MTFF. It sets a 3%-of-GDP medium-term deficit target and requires the Finance Minister to lay an annual fiscal-outlook statement before Parliament.
The 2025 target was met. The open question is whether the glide path holds to the 3% PFFRA target without revenue or spending action.

Like a household that hit its annual savings target. The trend is right; the question is whether next year stays on it. Hitting one target does not establish a glide path. Markets price the trajectory, not the single year.

PFFRA already provides the statutory frame. The next test is enforcement: whether the fiscal-adjustment mechanism is triggered if the glide path slips.

posts.text: RM14.79 billion withdrawn from EPF Akaun Fleksibel by 30 June 2025. 4.63 million members had made at least one withdrawal. EPF later found most use was for essentials. Akaun Fleksibel launched May 2024 as a permanent flexible-withdrawal facility.
Post-pandemic EPF withdrawal facilities have reduced the compound growth base for millions of retirement accounts unless replenished.
Akaun Fleksibel was framed as an emergency facility, but its design allows withdrawal at any time, for any reason, with no eligibility test.
Around 36% of active formal EPF members met the RM240,000 basic-savings benchmark in 2024. The new RIA framework targets RM390,000 as the new basic floor.
Calling it 'flexible savings' does not change the math. Ringgit withdrawn today and not replenished compound into a larger gap at retirement.
Like eating your seed corn in a drought. It solves today's hunger but cuts into next year's harvest. Withdrawn ringgit, unless replenished, no longer earn EPF dividends until retirement.

Akaun Fleksibel helps short-term liquidity; EPF data show most use was for essentials. Its scale also signals household-finance pressure that policy should address upstream.

The interoperability question is already half-answered: DuitNow QR is the national standard. The harder questions are about fees, BNPL exposure, and who is left out.

Adoption is not protection. The infrastructure works. The guardrails on merchant fees, BNPL supervision, and meaningful consent are still being assembled.

entries.headline: Gig Workers Act 872: SOCSO Coverage Extended, EPF Retirement Still Missing
entries.radarSignal: melaka to add up to seven nominated assemblymen after constitutional amendment, cm says no

posts.text: Act 872 creates Malaysia's first dedicated gig-worker legal framework, extending SOCSO self-employment coverage to platform workers.
Mandatory SOCSO accident and disability protection: platforms must register workers and remit contributions on their behalf.

EPF retirement contributions are NOT included in this first phase. The long-tail income gap remains unaddressed. Voluntary i-Saraan covered ~10.7% of self-employed workers by 2022. The new mandatory scheme does not extend to retirement.
DOSM Q1 2025: 17.23 million labour force, 16.70 million employed, 3.45 million informal. Gig workers fall inside the informal universe.
The 'no social-security protection' framing is now narrower. The remaining gap is retirement adequacy, which platforms still do not fund.

Like adding seatbelts but skipping the crumple zone. The cheapest accident protection is in place; long-term retirement protection is not. Accident insurance is the easiest gig-economy reform. Retirement adequacy is the hardest, and the new framework does not touch it.

Phase 1 establishes mandatory platform-collected SOCSO deductions. The open Phase 2 question is whether retirement-savings coverage follows, and on what timeline.

PADU compiled about 30.4 million individual profiles by June 2025. It serves as one of the key reference databases for MoF targeted-subsidy validation.

By Budget 2026, electricity-rationalisation savings averaged ~RM6 billion/year. Diesel rationalisation contributed substantially in 2024-25. Components have shifted as RON95 targeting begins. Read headline savings against verified component figures.
Subsidy effectiveness reporting is still done largely by implementing ministries. Independent per-cohort audits remain limited.
The savings number is now larger and better documented. Targeting-accuracy measurement by an independent party is the next test.

Like fixing a leaky pipe and announcing the savings before anyone independent has measured the new flow rate. Headline savings are useful but incomplete evidence of policy success until delivery accuracy is independently audited.

A reform proposal: stand up an independent audit publishing per-cohort delivery accuracy, separate from the implementing ministries' self-reporting.

posts.text: 42 died at sites where EIA rules were overridden. The mechanism is constitutional and most states refuse the reform that would fix it.

entries.headline: LCS Programme: RM6.08B Spent, First Ship in Sea Trials, Original Schedule 7 Years Late

posts.text: RM6.08 billion spent. Zero ships delivered to the Royal Malaysian Navy. The first vessel is in sea trials. LCS programme: contract signed 2011, first delivery due 2019. Original contract RM9.13B for 6 ships, revised to RM11.2B for 5 ships.

PAC identified RM1.4B in cost overruns and allocations used for purposes other than the LCS works. PAC also flagged 'pembayaran melebihi kerja sebenar' (payments exceeding actual work) under a progress-payment schedule weakly tied to milestones.
MACC investigation papers were completed by August 2022. The former BNS managing director was charged with CBT involving RM21M.

PAC and audit findings carry serious defence and maritime-enforcement implications. Patrol relies on MMEA, RMN assets and Op Naga. AG reporting cited 89 Chinese-vessel incursions from 2016-2019. The LCS shortfall is one input into a broader capability picture.
The question is no longer whether RM6B bought ships. It is whether the revised contract, new payment terms and trial timeline will close the gap they opened.

Like paying a builder RM6B against a RM9B contract, finding partial hulls instead of a delivered fleet, and renegotiating with the same builder. Independent oversight came from PAC, the National Audit Department, MACC and auditors, not from BNS itself.

Accountability did happen: PAC reports, declassification, MACC charges, contract restructure. The unresolved test is delivery and whether the new terms hold.

entries.headline: Gig Workers Act 2025: Mandatory SOCSO Registration; EPF Retirement Still Outside

posts.text: Act 872 makes platform-provider registration and PERKESO contribution mandatory for gig workers; EPF retirement is not included.

Voluntary opt-in retirement schemes have shown limited reach. EPF i-Saraan had 291,743 participants in 2022. DOSM 2022: 2.88 million own-account workers + 489,800 unpaid family workers. World Bank notes that i-Saraan take-up remained low despite increased outreach.
Employment Act section 101C creates a rebuttable presumption of employee/employer status. It does not exclude app-based engagement from the definition.
Accident SOCSO is mandatory under Act 872. Retirement and ordinary sick-leave income smoothing remain outside the Act.
Accident-related coverage closes the cheapest gap. Retirement income and ordinary illness income smoothing remain unaddressed.

Like fitting seatbelts but not building roads. The protection is real, the missing infrastructure is bigger. Workplace accidents are the easiest risk to insure. Long-tail risks like outliving savings are the hardest, and the framework does not touch them.

Act 872 is Malaysia's first dedicated gig-worker statute and a real adaptation. Section 7 allows further terms to be negotiated; the retirement gap remains open.
